checks: Recomputed ratios from ratios.csv integrals: CN1-0/HCN1-0 N 239.37/135.68=1.764, S 83.12/59.67=1.393, N/S 1.266; HNC/HCN 0.523/0.422; CN 3-2/1-0 0.155/0.103. Arithmetic agrees with report.json Q54a-c. Reproducing Ledger+2021 CN/HCN~1.7 at N is a good anchor.

Internal consistency: HNC/HCN(1-0) at 2.5" is 0.52/0.42 (00993) vs 0.44/0.36 (00412): a 15-18% difference for the SAME line pair from two projects, larger than quoted stat errors (1-2%). It is quoted but not understood (flux scale, missing flux in the 1.3" 00412 cubes, window). Likewise the CN 3-2/HCN 3-2 N/S double ratio drifts 1.15 -> 1.57 with beam (1.1-2.5"), i.e. CN 3-2 at S is not robust; this is stated but then 3-2 N/S 'CN 2.5-2.8x vs HCO+' is still used in the conclusion.

Not independently re-run from cubes (time); I checked the logic of the conclusion rather than the integrals. Key weakness: the headline claim 'S HCN deficit is shared by HNC, CN, CS, so HCO+ is the discrepant species' is only a ratio-of-ratios in Tb with HCN tau10~5-12 (Q47) and CN complex tau~0.8; opacity and abundance are not separated, so 'composition' vs 'excitation/opacity' is not actually tested. Confidence 'low' on Q54d is appropriate but the verdict text is stronger than the evidence.

CN 1-0 whole-complex integral compared with HCN 1-0 mixes two hyperfine groups with different opacity; the main-group-only ratio (1.10 N, 0.87 S) is below the 'non-SB 1.1' threshold at S, so whether S is CN-bright depends on the choice. The N/S ratio is the same (1.27), which is the robust part.
Model comparison is qualitative only (literature text, no grid run), whereas the question asks what the ratios say about PDR/XDR/mechanical heating.

fixes.what: Resolve the HNC/HCN(1-0) discrepancy between 2015.1.00993 and 2015.1.00412 (and HCN 1-0 between them: 135.7 vs 142.0 at N, 59.7 vs 61.5 at S): compare same-line integrals at identical beams, check missing flux with a uv-range-matched comparison (taper/restrict uv to the common baseline range for 00993 vs 00412 and for 2018.1.00223 CN vs HCN), and adopt one ratio with a systematic error that includes the spread.
fixes.why: The spread (15-18%) exceeds statistical errors by 10x and is comparable to the N/S contrasts (1.24) being interpreted; HNC/HCN N/S=1.24+-0.05 vs 0.99+-0.15 depends on which dataset/beam.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Match uv coverage (common uvmin/uvmax, same weighting/taper) before convolving to a common beam; report ratios from line pairs observed in the same SB/same spw where possible; propagate flux-scale and uv-coverage systematics into the final error.

fixes.what: Carry the ratios to physical quantities: run RADEX (the Q47 grid) for HCN, HNC, CN(with hyperfines if feasible) using the measured 1-0/3-2(/4-3) ratios to constrain Tkin, n and tau at N and S, then convert the line ratios to column-density ratios N(HNC)/N(HCN), N(CN)/N(HCN) with uncertainties, and with HCN/H13CN or HCO+/H13CO+ if the H13 cubes exist in the archive (check 2015.1.00993, 2016.2.00094).
fixes.why: Tb ratios at tau~5-12 are not abundance ratios; the conclusion 'composition not excitation' is otherwise untested, and N/S excitation differences (CN 3-2/1-0 x0.66, HCN 4-3/3-2 x0.6 at S) are directly in the data.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Non-LTE modelling of multi-J ratios (RADEX/LVG) to get column densities, then compare N ratios with PDR/XDR grids (Meijerink+2007, Loenen+2008 HNC/HCN vs Tkin, Ledger+2021 CN/HCN) at the derived n, T.

fixes.what: Quantify the model comparison: tabulate the actual ranges of HNC/HCN, CN/HCN, HCN/HCO+ from Meijerink+2007 XDR/PDR grids (n=1e5-1e6, relevant G0/F_X) and Loenen+2008, and state which regimes each nucleus falls in, instead of qualitative statements.
fixes.why: The question asks explicitly what the ratios say about PDR vs XDR vs mechanical heating; as written the answer is 'qualitative, low confidence'.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Overplot measured ratios on published diagnostic diagrams (CN/HCN vs HNC/HCN, HCN/HCO+ vs HNC/HCN) with the observed error boxes including opacity-corrected ranges.

fixes.what: Do the sub-arcsec N-core measurement that was identified as feasible: CN 1-0 at 0.29" (2018.1.00223 X4b) plus HCN 1-0 at 0.65" (and HNC 3-2/HCN 3-2 at 0.75"), convolved to ~0.7", and test whether CN/HCN and HNC/HCN at the N core differ from the 2.5" values; also the S nucleus in the same beam.
fixes.why: Beam dependence is already evident (CN/HCN 3-2 at S 0.90 -> 0.60 from 1.1 to 2.5"; HNC/HCN N/S 0.99 at 1.4" vs 1.24 at 2.5") so the 2.5" values blend nuclear and extended gas; AGN chemistry is expected to be a nuclear-scale effect at S.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Matched sub-arcsec beams, with the missing-flux check against the compact-config cubes; present ratios as a function of beam (as done in Q53) so scale dependence is explicit.

fixes.what: Soften/justify the conclusion: state explicitly that CN/HCN and HNC/HCN being lower at S than N is the opposite of the simple XDR prediction only if opacity and excitation are equal, and give both alternatives (HCO+ excess at S vs N-core enhancement of all N-bearing species) with a consequence for each that can be tested (e.g. HCO+/H13CO+, C18O/13CO, CS/C34S).
fixes.why: Ambiguity left unexploited; current text picks 'composition' while excitation differences are measured at S.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Enumerate hypotheses, derive their predicted N/S double ratios, compare with the observed ones.
